answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A trellis of referrals can raise the required lock for clusters that share funding or behavior, while a long-lived relic of successful work earns lower fees but cannot be copied to new identities. A nebula of fresh accounts therefore gains no immediate trust: the attacker must immobilize capital per identity and risks losing it, making a large Sybil swarm expensive to sustain.
